outcome: No resolution, disproof, or scope-narrowing case of the general Margulis conjecture on measure classification for diagonalizable actions in higher-rank groups was found since 26 January 2024; only work on related but distinct problems (entropy-symmetry tools, non-maximal torus rigidity predating the window, the separate Margulis-Zimmer normal-subgroup conjecture, Zimmer-program rigidity for lattice actions on manifolds, and the rank-one Furstenberg x2 x3 conjecture) was found.
summary: The bullet names 'Margulis conjecture – measure classification for diagonalizable actions in higher-rank groups,' which is the conjecture (also attributed jointly to Furstenberg, Katok-Spatzier, and Margulis) that any invariant and ergodic probability measure for a higher-rank diagonalizable (multi-parameter Cartan/torus) action on a locally homogeneous space G/Gamma is either supported on a lower-dimensional invariant homogeneous subset or is the natural (Haar-type) measure — the higher-rank analogue of Ratner's theorem for unipotent flows, absent an entropy or other extra hypothesis. Extensive searching (arXiv listings, Google-indexed web search, the current Wikipedia article and its linked Margulis biography) turned up no paper, preprint, or announcement since 26 January 2024 that proves, disproves, or narrows a genuine case of this exact statement. What did surface: (1) Einsiedler-Lindenstrauss, 'Rigidity of non-maximal torus actions...' (arXiv:2307.04163), which does prove a positive-entropy measure classification result for higher-rank actions on arithmetic quotients of forms of SL_2 — squarely on-topic, but posted 9 July 2023, before the frozen revision's date, so it is not an event in the window (and in any case a positive-entropy classification is a longstanding, separate strand from the unconditional general conjecture, which the Wikipedia bullet as worded points to); (2) Brown-Lee, 'Positive entropy actions by higher-rank lattices' (arXiv:2409.05991, Sept 2024), which proves rigidity for lattice actions on manifolds (a Zimmer-program-style question) rather than measure classification on homogeneous spaces for diagonalizable/Cartan actions — a related but distinct problem, not a case of this one; (3) a 2026 paper resolving the Margulis-Zimmer conjecture (arXiv:2607.17078), which is a normal-subgroup-structure conjecture for lattices, unrelated in substance to measure classification despite the shared name; (4) the Katok-Spatzier conjecture on Anosov actions being algebraic, which is again a distinct (though thematically adjacent) conjecture, still open; (5) Furstenberg's x2,x3 conjecture, a rank-one/different-setting analogue, still open, with recent survey/partial work (Austin et al., dimension-of-intersections results) that does not bear on the higher-rank statement. No AI system appears anywhere in this literature. Given the volume and specificity of adjacent activity found with no hit on the actual conjecture, and no digestion, survey, or Wikipedia update suggesting otherwise, I am reasonably confident the general conjecture remains open with no qualifying case settled in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue the Einsiedler-Lindenstrauss positive-entropy classification (2023, pre-window) or its style of result represents 'the' state of the art that any 2024+ paper builds incrementally on, and that some incremental strengthening inside papers like 2409.05991 or later citing works could count as a 'case' of the Margulis conjecture if one reads the bulleted conjecture loosely as encompassing entropy-assumption variants (which is how much of the literature actually studies this family of conjectures, since the unconditional statement is considered close to hopeless without an entropy or invariance hypothesis). Under that looser reading the correct status might be 'progress' rather than 'open'. I did not find any post-January-2024 entropy-classification paper that clearly extends 2307.04163's specific arithmetic-SL_2 result to new cases, so even under the looser reading no in-window event qualifies as a status-changing move.
what_would_settle_it: A dated arXiv submission or journal paper after 26 January 2024 that either proves the general Margulis/Furstenberg/Katok-Spatzier-style measure classification conjecture for higher-rank diagonalizable actions (with or without an entropy hypothesis, if the reader treats entropy-conditional results as in-scope cases), or that exhibits a genuinely new invariant measure violating the conjectured dichotomy in some higher-rank setting.
